cases.explanation: Syntactic structure, negation, deontic modality, temporal anchor, judicial setting, and argument order are accurately preserved from source to target.
Source expresses a negated obligation ('muss... nicht'), whereas target translates this as an affirmative obligation ('deve'), completely inverting the polarity.
Source specifies a negative integer value (−12 Euro), while target converts it into a positive quantity (12 euro), altering the arithmetic polarity of the transaction.
Source calendar date (10.11.2026) is shifted by one day in the target (11/11/2026).
Syntactic subject and thematic actor anchor are inverted; source positions Anna as agent/initiator meeting Bruno, whereas target positions Bruno as the syntactic subject meeting Anna.
Source modal verb 'darf' conveys deontic permission (allowed to go), whereas target uses 'deve', shifting the modal force to deontic necessity/obligation (must go).

Direct quotation with explicit quote marks is collapsed into indirect reported speech without quote markers; the quoted proposition's polarity is inverted ('wirkt nicht' becomes 'funziona'); speech act tense shifts from past ('sagte') to present ('afferma').
Legal disposition is inverted: source states acquittal ('freigesprochen'), while target states conviction ('condannato').

response.uncertainty: Surface heuristics may fail to detect pragmatically nuanced shifts; all evaluations are strictly bounded by source text semantics without extratextual validation.
